name: Scar Foot weekend
summary: A silent weekend on a fellside smallholding for eight people who already practise. No scheduled sits; the fell, the wood pile, the byre, and yourself. £60.
description:
Scar Foot is a smallholding at the foot of the Howgills with a converted byre that sleeps eight. We open it most weekends between March and October to people who already have a practice and want two days of silence somewhere with a hill.

There are no scheduled sits. The byre has cushions and a bell and people use them when they choose. Some sit at dawn and dusk because that is what they do at home. Some sit for three hours in the middle of the day and not otherwise. Some do not sit in the byre at all and spend both days on the fell, which is steep and open and takes most of a day to cross. People split wood; there is a great deal of it and the axe is by the door. Nobody will suggest anything, and nobody will notice what you do.

Silence is kept from Friday evening to Sunday lunch, including at meals, which are left in the byre kitchen for people to eat when they come in.

Jen lives in the farmhouse and is around. She does not teach and does not lead anything; on Friday evening she shows you where things are and then leaves you to it. If you want to talk, there is a slot on Saturday afternoon and you can put your name on the board. Most weekends nobody does.

It is moderately demanding. The fell is real, the wood is heavy, and the byre is cold at six in the morning. We assume everyone has done a silent retreat before and knows how to spend two entirely unstructured days without a teacher or a bell. This is not the place to learn that.
practical: Friday 6pm to Sunday 1pm, most weekends March to October. £60 including the byre and all food. Eight bunks in one room; bring a sleeping bag. Wood stove, hot water, one shower. Bring boots, waterproofs, gloves for the wood, and warm layers. Oxenholme station is fourteen miles; Jen collects on Friday at five. No signal.
